texts.facts: A-5) M/s Deepanshu Dairy Food Pvt Ltd, Village Butrara, Tehsil Shamli, Distt. Muzzaffarnagar U.P. ... Accused person. Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisi ons of the PFA Act and Rules . 2. As per the complaint, on 21.04.2007 the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh Gian Chand and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Sh J.P. Bhardwaj alongwith staff and under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM Sh Yogesh Pratap visited the premises of M/s Bansal Store, Khasra No. 818/2, Main Road, Burari, Delhi, where the accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal was found conducting the business of DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc above said shop, having stored various food articles including Ghee (Madhvan Brand) for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Ghee (Madhvan Brand) from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted of 3 sealed plastic jars of 2 litre each having identical label declaration and batch no. as reproduced on Form VI. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of SDM/LHA Sh Yogesh Pratap. One sample counterpart was taken as a one sealed plastic jar. Each sample jar was separately, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act & Rules. The vendor's signature were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample jar. Notice in form VI was given to the accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal and the price of the sample was also given to him vide receipt dated 21.04.2007. Panchanama was prepared at the spot. Notice in Form VI was also prepared against the supplier of the sample commodity. All the documents prepared by FI were signed by the accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal as well as the witness FA Sh J.P. Bhardwaj. Before taking sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such FA Sh J.P. Bhardwaj was joined as witness. 3. One counterpart of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 41/LHA/18441 was sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter parts of the sample were deposited with SDM/LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be non- conforming to standards. The report of the PA is as follows :- Da vs Vinod Kumar Bansal Etc on 24 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106232581/ 2 DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc "The sample does not conform to standard because (1) BR exceeds to prescribed maximum limit of 43 (2) BT is Positive which should be negative in Ghee (3) Reichert value is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 28. The sample is also misbranded because language of Best before is not as per PFA Act & Rules and also it is declared in a misleading manner. 4. It is further the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal is the vendor-cum-proprietor of accused M/s Bansal Store, Khasra No. 818/2, Main Road, Burari, Delhi at the time of sampling and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. The vendor purchased the said food articles from M/s Goyal Traders, 78, Punjabi Colony, Narela, Delhi 40, which is a proprietorship concern in the name of accused No. 2 Lachman Das and he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of business of the said shop. M/s Goyal Traders had godown at 2044, Nai Basti Narela, Delhi - 40. Accused No. 2 Lachman Das Proprietor of Goyal Traders had disclosed that he had purchased the sample commodity from manufacturing company accused No. 5 M/s Deepanshu Dairy Food Pvt Ltd, Village Butrara, Tehsil, Shamli, Distt. Muzzaffarnagar U.P. The said company is having two directors i.e accused No. 3 Surender Kumar Khandelwal and accused No. 4 Rajni Khandelwal. Both the Directors of the company were incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the company. Being a company M/s Deepanshu Dairy Food P Ltd is also liable. DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 17.09.2007 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(m) & section 2(ix)(g)(k) of PFA Act and also Rule 32(f)(i) & Rule 37 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused persons. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 17.09.2007. Based on the report of the PA as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(m), 2(ix)(k)(g) of PFA Act 1954 and Rule 32(f)(i) and Rule 37 of PFA Rules, 1955 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial, accused No. 2 passed away and proceedings against him were abated vide order dated 09.01.2014. Accused No. 4 was also discharged vide order dated 12.05.2016 and accused No. 3 Surender Kumar was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 04.12.2017 in the present case. Accused no. 5 company was proceeded ex parte. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Gian Chand, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh Yogesh Pratap and PW-3 FA J.P. Bhardwaj. PW-1 and PW-3 DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Yogesh Pratap. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of three sealed plastic jars of Ghee (Madhvan Da vs Vinod Kumar Bansal Etc on 24 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106232581/ 3 Brand) of two liters each, bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by taking one sealed plastic jar as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. A notice u/s 14A Ex.PW1/B1 was prepared at the spot addressing to M/s Goyal Traders and was sent through registered post on the next working day. The vendor also furnished his statement Ex.PW1/D1 alongwith document Mark X to X-2 Report under Rule 9(e) Ex.PW1/D-1 was also prepared at the spot. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in another sealed cover were sent separately to PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/E on 23.04.2007 and remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 23.04.2007 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/F. Thereafter PW-1 FI Gian Chand sent a Letter to Agmark Office, Delhi vide Ex. PW 1/G through registered office, informing that I had lifted a sample of Ghee, on the label of which there was 'Agmark Logo' & 'Agmark Number'. DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW 1/H was received according to which the sample was not conforming to the standards as well as misbranded and misleading. Thereafter, on the directions of SDM/LHA, PW-1 FI Gian Chand started the investigation and during investigations, the Notice U/s 14 A of PFA Act, sent to M/s Goyal Traders was received back 'undelivered' with the remark of the Postal Department that 'no such firm was there at Premises No. 2044, Nayi Basti, Narela, Delhi vide Ex.PW1/M and the envelope Ex.PW1/l-1. Thereafter, PW-1 FI Gian Chand sent a letter and reminder to the vendor Ex. PW 1/J and Ex. PW 1/J-1 through registered post and received the reply Ex. PW 1/J-2 alongwith documents Mark X-3 to X-7. He also sent a letter Ex. PW1/K to VATO, Ward No. 72 seeking information on the constitution of M/s Bansal Store and received its reply stating that the said firm was a proprietorship Firm having accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal as its Proprietor. Thereafter PW -1 sent a Letter Ex.PW1/L to M/s Goyal Traders and received back undelivered. Thereafter two reminders Ex. PW1/L-1 and Ex. PW 1/L-2 were sent and received reply Ex.PW1/L-3 alongwith documents Mark X-8 Mark X-9. He also sent a letter Ex.PW1/M to VATO, Ward No. 71 seeking information on the constitution of M/s Goyal Traders and received its reply. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex. PW1/N to Senior Marketing Officer, Agmark Office, Delhi seeking information on the constitution of Deepanshu Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd. and received its reply Ex.PW1/N-1 alongwith list of director Mark X-10. Thereafter PW-1 sent a Letter Ex.PW1/O and reminder Ex. PW 1/O-1 to Debpanshu Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd. through registered post and received the reply DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc Ex. PW1/O-2 alongwith document Mark X-11 to Mark X-16. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/P to CMO, Muzaffarnagar and received its reply Ex.PW1/P-1 aiongwith documents Mark X- 17 & X-18. Vide letter Ex.PW1/P-1 nomination of nominee Shri Dinesh Sharma of Deepanshu Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd. was accepted on 03.02.2007. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/Q to Shri Dinesh Sharma regarding confirmation of his Nomination and received its reply Ex.PW1/Q-1 aiongwith document Mark X-19. PW-1 also received Ex.PW1/O-2 a reply from CMO, Muzaffarnagar stating that there was no nominee of Deepanshu Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd. till 17.01.2007. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex. PW1/R to Lacchman Dass proprietor of M/s Goyal Traders asking the said person to furnish the documentary evidence for purchase of sample commodity from Deepanshu Dairy Foods Pvt. Ltd. as the photocopy of Bill supplied earlier by him was not connected with the sample commodity. In response of the same, Da vs Vinod Kumar Bansal Etc on 24 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106232581/ 4 Shri Lacchman Dass handed over to him an Affidavit vide Ex. PW1/R-1 wherein, he disclosed that he was the Distributor of Madhvan Ghee, manufactured by Deepanshu Diary Foods Pvt. Ltd. and the Bill of the purchase of the sample commodity was not available with him. After completion of investigation the entire case file was put before the concerned SDM/LHA who forwarded the same to the then Director of PFA for obtaining the sanction and the then Director PFA Sh N. Balachandran granted his consent for prosecution against the accused persons vide Ex.PW1/S. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW-1/T was filed in the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/U alongwith copy of PA Reports were sent to accused persons through DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc post vide postal receipt Mark X-20. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 06.01.2018 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In defence evidence, the accused No. 1 Vinod Kumar Bansal examined himself as DW-1 and proved the bill in his favour by accused no. 2 as DW1/A.
texts.arguments: the defence has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State 2009(1) FAC 132 to argue that there was a policy of the complainant department of 1985 numbered as Policy No F6(228)/85/ENF/PFA wherein a decision was taken to give a written warning to the offenders with regard to any deficiency in respect of Rule 32 of the PFA Act. Although, no DA vs Vinod Kumar Bansal etc such policy has been placed or proved on record by other side and this policy was further withdrawn as per the aforesaid judgment on the ground that Section 20 of the PFA Act does not confer any such power on the consenting authority to issue such warning to the vendors found violating Rule 32 of the PFA Act. The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011 and recently in Hello Minerals Water PVT LTD & Ors vs State CRL.MC.224/2016 dated 10.01.2018. 15.Be that as it may, PFA Act or Rules does not provide any such warning but since the benefit of this policy has been given in the case of S.S. Gokul Krishnan (referred above), I feel myself bound by the ratio of that case.
